name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels; an electric one whose motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) is a full motorcycle rather than a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Kansas Statutes Annotated §8-1438 and §8-126(x).

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground; excludes electric-assisted bicycles
Its motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W); one at or below that is a motor-driven cycle
A vehicle exceeding any motorized bicycle limit is titled and registered as a motorcycle
Riders need a class M driver's license
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a motorcycle helmet
The operator must wear shatterproof eye protection unless it has a windscreen at least 10 inches tall, and passengers under 18 must wear it regardless
Titled and registered, and must carry motor vehicle liability insurance

Kansas has no off-highway motorcycle category: its all-terrain vehicle definition needs three or more tires, so a two-wheeled off-road e-moto is still a motorcycle and can't be ridden on a highway unless registered
